title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Fig. 1b-j (Results: Joint kinematics suggest that hindlegs dominate MDN-triggered backward walking); Supplementary Movies 1-2
quote: we found that the adult MDNs drive coordinated changes in stepping patterns across all three pairs of legs, with the strongest impact on the hindlegs
mapping_basis: Paper's name MDN (Moonwalker Descending Neuron) is the MANC type name MDN; driver MDN-1-GAL4 (VT044845-ZpGAL4DBD; VT050660-p65ADZp) is listed in driver_lines.csv as MDN-1 -> MDN.
stimulation: 660 nm laser, 5-s constant red light, ~0.73 mW/mm2
frequency_note: Per-leg stepping frequency in intact flies before amputation (Fig. 1j source data) roughly 0.4-4.3 Hz across flies and legs. Amputated hindlegs oscillated at ~6 Hz.
coordination_notes: Phase coupling of coxa-trochanter and femur-tibia flexion/extension reversed relative to forward walking; hindlegs provide main propulsion (hindleg tarsal amputation abolishes backward walking, but amputated legs keep oscillating).
n_flies_note: N = 7 flies for Fig. 1b-h; n = 6 flies per amputation group (Fig. 1i,j)
notes: Flies were first allowed to walk forward spontaneously, then the light triggered backward walking (direction reversal); effect_on_walking has no 'reverses' option, so it is set to not_assessed. Leg joints were tracked with DeepLabCut for all three legs on one side. Amputation sub-experiment (Fig. 1i,j) is included here because it uses the same figure, line and preparation.

title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Supplementary Fig. 5a,c (Supplementary Information p. 6); Results section 'LBL40 neurons trigger tibia flexion via the tibia-reductor motor neurons'
quote: optogenetic activation of the severed VNC projections of the MDNs induces backward walking, with its characteristically exaggerated hindleg movements (Supplementary Fig. 5)
mapping_basis: Paper's name MDN is the MANC type name; genotype for Supplementary Fig. 5 is MDN-1-GAL4 (VT044845-ZpGAL4DBD; VT050660-p65ADZp), listed in driver_lines.csv as MDN-1 -> MDN.
stimulation: 660 nm laser, 5-s constant red light, ~0.73 mW/mm2
frequency_note: Backward step frequency in decapitated flies (Supp. Fig. 5c source data means): hindleg ~1.25 Hz, midleg ~1.2 Hz, foreleg ~1.4 Hz; all lower than intact flies (hind ~2.2, mid ~1.9, fore ~3.5 Hz).
n_flies_note: Legend: N = 7 flies per group (the source data list 8 values for the decapitated group)
notes: A tethered decapitated fly is described as normally stationary, so backward stepping starts with the stimulus. Supp. Fig. 5a joint-angle traces show repeated cycles in fore-, mid- and hindlegs during the 5-s light, and Supp. Fig. 5c quantifies step frequency for each leg.

title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Supplementary Fig. 5b,c (Supplementary Information p. 6), intact flies
quote: Representative time series of joint angles in a decapitated (a) and intact (b) MDN>CsChrimson fly. Red bars indicate the 5-s red light stimulation.
mapping_basis: Paper's name MDN is the MANC type name; genotype is MDN-1-GAL4 (VT044845-ZpGAL4DBD; VT050660-p65ADZp), listed in driver_lines.csv as MDN-1 -> MDN.
stimulation: 660 nm laser, 5-s constant red light, ~0.73 mW/mm2
frequency_note: Backward step frequency in intact flies (Supp. Fig. 5c source data means): hindleg ~2.2 Hz, midleg ~1.9 Hz, foreleg ~3.5 Hz.
notes: figure: the result is shown in the Supplementary Fig. 5 legend and panels (supplementary PDF), not in text.txt; the quote is the legend text. Same genotype and preparation as record a5-g20-B-0001 (Fig. 1) but a separate figure, coded separately per PROTOCOL section 1. The intact comparison group for the headless record a5-g20-B-0002. Panel b shows repeated stepping cycles in all three legs during the light.

title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Fig. 4b and Supplementary Fig. 3b (negative-control genotype: empty split-GAL4 > TNT), Fly Bowl
quote: Robust backward walking was observed upon MDN activation in negative control flies, but completely abolished in both of the positive controls (Fig. 4b).
mapping_basis: Paper's name MDN is the MANC type name. The split-LexA driver (VT049484-ZpLexADBD; VT050660-p65ADZp) is not in driver_lines.csv; the paper says it labels MDNs and MANs.
stimulation: 627 nm whole-arena light, nine 5-s pulses at 60-s intervals, three each at 0.158, 0.288 and 0.456 mW/mm2
sensory_condition: Fly Bowl open arena, groups of ~25 flies, backlit IR
n_flies_note: typically ~50 flies per genotype across two trials
notes: Methods: the split-LexA 'expressed in both MDNs and MANs but no other central neurons'. Backward walking was scored from centroid tracking (Ctrax forward/backward speed), with no leg tracking, so per-leg rhythm follows the walking convention and confidence is medium. The negative control also expresses TNT under an empty split-GAL4 (no expression). MDN activation combined with TNT silencing of MF cells (the other genotypes in Fig. 4b) is not coded as a separate MDN record. Proposed driver-line row added.

title: Distributed control of motor circuits for backward walking in Drosophila.
source_locator: Fig. 7a-g control trials (red light only) and Supplementary Fig. 7; Methods 'Behavioral assays'; Supplementary Movies 10-11
quote: For SS > GtACR2 neuronal epistasis experiments, we first tested if a decapitated fly could walk backwards steadily during the 25-s red-light stimulus.
mapping_basis: Paper's name MDN is the MANC type name. Fig. 7 genotype uses the MDN split-LexA (VT049484-ZpLexADBD; VT050660-p65ADZp), not in driver_lines.csv; the paper says it labels MDNs and MANs.
stimulation: 660 nm laser, 25-s red light, ~0.73 mW/mm2 (control trials without blue light)
frequency_note: Hindleg step frequency in control trials of Empty-SS flies (Fig. 7g source data) ~0.55-1.16 Hz, mean ~0.77 Hz.
penetrance: Only flies with stable baseline backward walking during the 25-s red light were further tested (selection step).
n_flies_note: 8 (Empty-SS), 9 (SS47938) and 8 (SS50974) flies in Fig. 7c-g, plus positive-control flies in Fig. 7b
notes: Only hindleg joint angles and hindleg steps were tracked and quantified in Fig. 7, so fore- and midleg rhythm are not_assessed. Females only (Methods). The GtACR2 effector in other cells is off in control trials. Confidence is medium because flies were pre-selected for stable backward walking. The same driver labels MANs (Methods).

title: A dedicated brain circuit controls forward walking in Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 5c,d; Supplementary Fig. 5a,c; Results 'Walking drive is flexibly suppressed or integrated'; Supplementary Video 7
quote: Strikingly, MDN-activated flies always walked backward, rendering flies unable to cross the gap (Fig. 5c,d and Supplementary Fig. 5a).
mapping_basis: Paper names 'Moonwalker descending neurons (MDN or DNp50)'; MDN is the MANC type name and DNp50 is a listed synonym. Driver VT044845-GAL4.DBD; VT050660-p65.AD = MDN-1 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm red LEDs, 1-s pulse triggered manually before (phase 0) or during (phases 1-3) gap crossing; intensity not stated
sensory_condition: gap-crossing assay, wings clipped, two platforms 3.5 mm apart in water-filled arena, white light
penetrance: always walked backward (Supp. Fig. 5a: backward in ~100% of trials in phases 0-3, apart from a few falls)
n_flies_note: N = 4-13 flies per phase (phase 0: 4 flies, 4 trials); 13 flies in Fig. 5d
notes: Behaviour was annotated manually from side-view video (walking backward vs climbing etc.), with no leg tracking, so confidence is medium. In phase 0 flies were standing in front of the gap and moving flies were excluded, so stimulation of standing flies elicited backward walking. Latency to move was ~0.35 s (Supp. Fig. 5c). In phase 3, activation drove flies backward into the water.
